task.name: Whether a model has demonstrated a capability is established only by an operator-invoked probe that persists nothing, so routing cannot consult it and must assume capability at dispatch
task.story_text:
## Why

Whether a model can serve a capability is knowable and is never recorded. The readiness check that
establishes it exercises the capability correctly, reports the result to whoever ran it, and persists
nothing. Nothing at dispatch time can consult it, so routing assigns work on the assumption that any
eligible model can serve whatever the phase requires.

The consequence is that a capability mismatch is discovered by failing. A role whose result is only
usable when structured is assigned to a model that cannot produce structured output, the phase
returns something unusable, and the gate depending on it reports an absence it cannot explain. The
operator learns the model could not do the job from the wreckage rather than from the routing
decision, and learns it again on the next dispatch, because nothing was written down.

This gap is what makes the adjacent work unimplementable rather than merely unfinished. A story
asking assignment to consult a demonstrated capability was refused at preflight for exactly this
reason: the spec requires a recorded fact, and the only mechanism that establishes the fact is a
manual probe that no runtime path reads.

The distinction being drawn is between reporting to a person and recording for a system. The existing
check does the first well. What is missing is that its findings outlive the invocation that produced
them and are readable by the component that decides where work goes.

## Example

What routing can answer today, and what it should be able to answer:

```
today
  assignment: is this model eligible for the review phase?     yes  (from configuration)
  assignment: can this model return a structured result?       unknown — assume yes
  outcome:    dispatched, returns prose, gate reports nothing usable

wanted
  assignment: can this model return a structured result?       demonstrated: no, as of <when>
  outcome:    not dispatched to a role that requires it; the routing rationale says why
```

The operator-facing difference is that "this model was not chosen because it has not demonstrated it
can return a structured result" appears in the routing decision, instead of an empty recommendation
appearing at a gate an hour later.

## Acceptance criteria

- Exercising a model writes the capability outcome somewhere durable, keyed to the identity that was
  exercised, and records when it was established.
- The component that assigns work reads that record and can distinguish three states for any
  identity and capability: demonstrated, demonstrated to be absent, and never established.
- Never established is not treated as absent. An identity with no record remains eligible, so
  introducing this record does not silently narrow the pool to whatever has been probed.
- Where an assignment is declined because a capability was demonstrated absent, the routing rationale
  reports that reason, so it appears with the decision rather than in a later failure.
- A recorded outcome that predates a change to the identity it describes is not presented as current;
  the record either updates or reports its own staleness.

## Out of scope

Deciding which capabilities are worth recording beyond the one that motivated this, and any change to
how the readiness check exercises a model. This issue is about the fact outliving the probe and being
readable at dispatch, not about what the probe does.

handoff.summary: Added a durable capability-evidence store (.forge/model_capabilities.yaml) in a new model_capabilities.py module, keyed by canonical identity (provider/model/transport) plus capability and stamped with established_at. The readiness probe now classifies each attempt's capability outcome independently of its overall readiness status — only an attempt that actually validated structured output establishes the capability, an unsupported tool-request shape establishes absence, a CLI structured success survives an unavailable cost figure, and every attempt is keyed by the transport it exercised. check-providers persists that evidence. assign_models and apply_post_plan_checkpoint take an optional capability_records input and resolve per-role filtered candidate pools once before scoring, so first pick, tier/auth/pool-exhaustion fallbacks, dev exploration, and the budget enforcer's cheaper-model search all draw from the same pool; a candidate is skipped only on a current demonstrated absence. Exclusions surface as the canonical capability_demonstrated_absent reason with capability and established_at detail in routing_decision candidate_pool, and in the role rationale. Explicit operator pins are honored but flagged. The coordinator loads the record outside the adaptive guard at both assignment boundaries.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Never established is not treated as absent. An identity with no record remains eligible, so introducing this record does not silently narrow the pool to whatever has been probed.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Missing identity, missing capability, empty record and unreadable record all return never_established. test_never_established_candidate_stays_eligible asserts routing is byte-identical to the no-record baseline.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Where an assignment is declined because a capability was demonstrated absent, the routing rationale reports that reason, so it appears with the decision rather than in a later failure.
acceptance_criteria.notes: New canonical exclusion reason capability_demonstrated_absent with detail {capability, established_at, probe_detail, probe_role} on the candidate_pool entry, plus a rationale fragment naming the excluded models and when it was established. Covered by test_routing_decision_reports_the_reason_with_the_decision.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A recorded outcome that predates a change to the identity it describes is not presented as current; the record either updates or reports its own staleness.
acceptance_criteria.notes: A probe-subject signature (endpoint / CLI binary alongside the canonical identity) is stored; a lookup with a differing signature is flagged stale and current_absent is False, so it does not exclude. A re-probe overwrites the same record. Covered by test_changed_probe_subject_reports_stale_and_does_not_exclude, test_reprobe_updates_the_same_record, test_stale_record_does_not_exclude.

story_deviations: Plan step 2 said to persist ReadinessResult.declared_attempt outcomes mapped from readiness status. Implemented instead as an attempt-level capability verdict set by the probe itself, for every attempt including alternate transports — following the plan reviewer's P1: readiness status is not a capability fact (dev/preflight READY validates nothing; a CLI structured success with unavailable cost is UNVERIFIED but did demonstrate the capability). Merge across multiple role probes for one identity+capability is deterministic: absent wins over demonstrated within a batch.

Plan step 1 named AgentDef.provider_family; that property does not exist. Separate typed adapters were added — identity_for_profile (ModelProfile.provider_family/.mode) and identity_for_agent (AgentDef.effective_provider + TransportSpec.kind).
deferred_items: Explicit operator pins (explicit_profiles and spliced explicit reviewer pools) are never blocked on a demonstrated absence — operator intent wins, consistent with explicit_override_locked semantics elsewhere. They are flagged instead: a WARNING in the role rationale and a capability_warning on the spliced pool entry. Blocking operator pins would be a policy change beyond this story's scope.

When a role's entire candidate pool is demonstrated-absent, the unfiltered pool is used as a last resort with an explicit WARNING in the rationale rather than seating nobody — mirroring the module's existing auth/tier-floor fallbacks. An alternative (empty reviewer panel / refusal) is a separate policy decision.

handoff.summary: Iteration 1 fixes the single P1: the all-candidates-absent fallback restored the unfiltered pool and seated demonstrated-absent models for planner and reviewer roles. _capability_pool now returns the filtered pool as-is including when empty, and assign_models raises NoCapableCandidateError (a ValueError, joining the module's existing unroutable-pool contract) before any selection runs when the record rules out every candidate for a role — naming the role, the capability, and when each absence was established. Explicitly pinned roles remain exempt because they never reach candidate selection; apply_post_plan_checkpoint needs no refusal because it is an optional demotion that preserves the seated dev when no capable cheaper candidate exists. Iteration 0 (still in the diff) added the durable store itself: model_capabilities.py holding .forge/model_capabilities.yaml keyed by canonical identity (provider/model/transport) plus capability and stamped with established_at, three lookup states with separate staleness reporting, an attempt-level capability verdict on the readiness probe that is independent of readiness status, persistence from check-providers, per-role filtered candidate pools threaded through every selection path in assign_models, and coordinator loading outside the adaptive guard at both assignment boundaries.

reviews.summary: [openai-gpt-5.5-cli] Routing still seats demonstrated-absent models when every candidate for a required capability is absent. | [google-gemini-3.5-flash-api] Added durable model capabilities tracking and consulted it at routing to avoid mismatches at dispatch. | [anthropic-claude-haiku-4-5-cli] The implementation satisfies all five acceptance criteria with sound design: durable capability storage keyed by identity + capability, correct state discrimination (demonstrated / absent / never-established), proper staleness handling via subject signatures, and comprehensive coordinator integration. Capability filtering is applied consistently across all routing paths (first-pick, fallbacks, budget downgrades, post-plan checkpoint) in both adaptive and static modes. Test coverage is thorough and includes seam-level integration tests across the probe → evidence → store → routing boundaries. No P1 issues identified.

findings.description: When every candidate for a structured role is recorded as demonstrated absent, routing restores the unfiltered pool and seats those models for planner and reviewer work.

Covered by tests/test_model_capabilities.py:122, tests/test_model_capabilities.py:182, and tests/test_capability_routing_seam.py:417.; src/theforge/model_capabilities.py:448-453 checks signature difference and sets stale=True which makes current_absent return false; tested in tests/test_capability_routing_seam.py:363-373 and tests/test_model_capabilities.py:143-167.; Iteration 0 (still in diff). src/theforge/model_capabilities.py lines 195–213 (_signature hashes endpoint/CLI); lines 299–308 (lookup checks subject_signature and sets stale=True on mismatch); CapabilityLookup.current_absent (lines 258–261) returns False when stale. tests/test_model_capabilities.py test_changed_probe_subject_reports_stale_and_does_not_exclude, test_stale_record_does_not_exclude verify stale records don't exclude.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 2 assumes readiness statuses are capability facts, but the actual API disproves that. provider_readiness.py:546-554 labels dev and preflight probes plain-structured/tool-structured while _requires_structured_verdict at 616-617 deliberately accepts unstructured output for those phases, so READY does not demonstrate the named structured capability. Conversely, lines 365-386 validate structured output and then classify a CLI result with unavailable cost as UNVERIFIED, so the proposed rule would discard a capability that was demonstrated. Agent-pool roles at lines 577-604 also produce multiple differently validated probes for the same identity+capability key, allowing them to overwrite one another. This carries the plan's first stated risk and makes the durable fact unreliable.
  Suggestion: Persist a capability-specific result independent of overall readiness/cost status. Only a probe that actually validates structured output should establish structured capability, preserve CLI structured success despite unavailable cost, and define deterministic merging when several role probes address the same identity+capability. Add tests based on the existing unstructured-preflight and CLI-cost-unavailable cases.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 3's filtering surface is incomplete. After _pick_agent/_select_reviewers run, _enforce_budget at assignment.py:1524-1544 can replace planner, dev, or reviewer profiles with the first cheaper agent without capability filtering; _apply_dev_exploration at 3132-3140 builds its challenger pool from every authed agent; and coordinator/preflight.py:1477-1492 splices full explicit reviewer pools into the final decision after assign_models, with reconcile_explicit_reviewer_pools subsequently marking them included. Explicit single-role profiles also bypass candidate selection. An absent identity can therefore still be dispatched and its routing evidence can say it was included. The fallback tests described in Step 6 do not enumerate these paths. This carries the plan's third stated risk on an acceptance-critical surface.
  Suggestion: Apply the capability predicate to budget downgrade candidates, exploration candidates, explicit profiles, and the full explicit-pool splice/reconciliation path, or perform a final capability validation of every seated profile before returning AssignmentDecision. Add focused tests for cost-cap downgrade, exploration, explicit single profiles, and multi-reviewer explicit pools.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 2 persists only ReadinessResult.declared_attempt, but run_readiness_probe exercises both declared and alternate transports by default. Transport kind is part of canonical identity, so a successful or absent alternate attempt is evidence for a distinct exercised identity that the plan explicitly drops.
  Suggestion: Persist every attempt that actually established a capability outcome, keyed by that attempt's attempted_transport_kind; retain declared-only behavior only when --declared-only prevented the alternate exercise.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 1 names AgentDef.provider_family as an identity input, but AgentDef has no such property in config/models.py:132-179. Its cross-transport provider property is effective_provider; ModelProfile is the type exposing provider_family.
  Suggestion: Define separate typed identity adapters: ModelProfile.provider_family and AgentDef.effective_provider, both combined with model and the normalized transport kind.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 4 says to load .forge/model_capabilities.yaml 'beside the existing model_profiles.yaml reads'. In src/theforge/coordinator/plan_flow.py:634-647 that read sits inside if _adaptive_enabled: — capability records are not a learning signal but a hard eligibility fact, so nesting the load there would silently disable demonstrated-absent blocking in static routing mode.
  Suggestion: Load the capability record outside the _adaptive_enabled guard in plan_flow.py (and unconditionally in preflight.py:1350) so the demonstrated-absent predicate applies in both static and adaptive modes.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Stated risk 3 (fallback paths bypass candidate filtering) is retired at the mitigation level — it enumerates _pick_agent (assignment.py:741), reviewer selection (_reviewer_candidate_pool, assignment.py:1871), dev fallback branches, and post-plan rerouting — but Step 6's test list names only the ordinary exclusion/eligibility cases, not a fallback-path case. The candidate-pool-exhaustion fallbacks at assignment.py:3699 and :3766 are exactly where the predicate is easiest to miss.
  Suggestion: Add one explicit test in tests/test_assignment_routing_decision.py that drives a demonstrated-absent candidate through the pool-exhaustion fallback branch and asserts it is still not seated.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 2 maps READINESS_STATUS_FAILED to demonstrated-absent. Verified this is defensible — provider_readiness.py:317-361 routes transport/auth/setup failures to unverified via _runtime_unverified_reason, so failed means the probe ran and the model produced an unusable result. But READINESS_STATUS_FAILED at :373 ('no valid verdict in structured output') and :331 (unclassified exception) reach the same status by different routes.
  Suggestion: Store the readiness detail string alongside the absent outcome so an operator can tell a structured-output failure from an unclassified exception when the routing rationale cites the record.
- [P1-impl] [google-gemini-3.5-flash-api] Determining whether a phase requires a structured verdict should match the logic in the provider_readiness check (e.g. non-dev/non-preflight phases like review/plan_review require structured outputs, or checking if the phase specifies allowed_tools).

finding_registry.description: When every candidate for a structured role is recorded as demonstrated absent, routing restores the unfiltered pool and seats those models for planner and reviewer work.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
